Here I will walk through cleaning and feature engineering the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet. We will run this for each tab separately to create a Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet Clean version with 3 tabs.

Workflow overview

-   Standardize units of all concentration variables to uM

-   Create new numeric variables:

    -   Total bioavailable element

    -   Relative proportion of bioavailable element

-   Create new categorical variables

    -   From numeric inherent stream characteristics (development, distance from main stem, drainage area, and relative elevation)

## II. Unit Conversions

Convert molar concentrations to uM and nM

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 1) If you have *_uM but not *_M, create *_M
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    across(
      matches("_uM$", ignore.case = FALSE),
      ~ .x * 1e-6,
      .names = "{str_remove(.col, '_uM$')}_M"
    ),

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 2) From *_M create *_uM and *_nM (case-sensitive, so _m won't match)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    across(
      matches("_M$", ignore.case = FALSE),
      list(uM = ~ .x * 1e6, nM = ~ .x * 1e9),
      .names = "{str_remove(.col, '_M$')}_{.fn}"
    ),

    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    # 3) Keep BL-bound conversions as-is
    # ---------------------------------------------------------
    across(
      ends_with("_mol_kg_Zn"),
      list(umol_g_Zn = ~ .x * 1e3, nmol_g_Zn = ~ .x * 1e6),
      .names = "{str_remove(.col, '_mol_kg_Zn$')}_{.fn}"
    ),
    across(
      ends_with("_mol_kg_Cu"),
      list(umol_g_Cu = ~ .x * 1e3, nmol_g_Cu = ~ .x * 1e6),
      .names = "{str_remove(.col, '_mol_kg_Cu$')}_{.fn}"
    )
  )
```

Checks

```{r}
# No duplicate column names
anyDuplicated(names(dat))

# Elevation should NOT have uM/nM/M versions
names(dat)[grepl("Relative_elevation_m_", names(dat))]
```

## III. Create New Numeric Variables

### i. Total Bioavailable Element

Total biotic ligand (TBL)-bound trace elements = TBL-element+ TBL-element hydroxide

```{r}
# TBL-Zn
dat$TBL_Zn_nmol_g <- dat$BL_Zn_nmol_g_Zn + dat$BL_ZnOH_nmol_g_Zn

# TBL-Cu
dat$TBL_Cu_nmol_g <- dat$BL_Cu_nmol_g_Cu + dat$BL_CuOH_nmol_g_Cu

# Check
hist(dat$TBL_Zn_nmol_g)
hist(dat$TBL_Cu_nmol_g)
```

### i. Relative Proportion of Bioavailable Element

Relative proportion of element (rel_prop_Zn_nM) = TBL-element / measured element

```{r}
# Zinc
dat$rel_prop_Zn <- dat$Free_Zn_uM / dat$Zn_uM

# Copper
dat$rel_prop_Cu <- dat$Free_Cu_uM / dat$Cu_uM

# Check
hist(dat$rel_prop_Zn)
hist(dat$rel_prop_Cu)
```

## IV. Create New Categorical Variables

### i. Stream Type

Distinguish tributaries from the EFPC main stem (within the EFK network)

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Type = if_else(
      Network == "EFK",
      "Main Stem",
      "Tributaries"
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("Main Stem", "Tributaries"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Type)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Type))
```

### ii. Orientation

As a proxy for bedrock lithology:

-   North slope

    -   Networks: BSL, WBK, MCA, MTN, NBO

-   South slope

    -   Networks: S_TRIB

-   Main stem

    -   Networks: EFK

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Orientation = case_when(
      Network %in% c("WBK", "MCA", "MTN", "NBO", "BSL") ~ "North slope",
      Network %in% c("S_TRIB") ~ "South slope",
      Network %in% c("EFK") ~ "Main stem",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% 
      factor(levels = c("North slope", "South slope", "Main stem"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Orientation)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Orientation))
```

### i. Development

Categorizing developed land use and land cover (LULC) will be based on a modified version of the MRLC National Land Cover Database Class Legend and Description. Our categories will be as follows

-   \<49% developed LULC = low intensity

-   50-79% developed LULC = medium intensity

-   \>80% developed LULC = high intensity

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Development = case_when(
      Developed_lulc < 50 ~ "Low",
      Developed_lulc >= 50 & Developed_lulc < 80 ~ "Medium",
      Developed_lulc >= 80 ~ "High"
    ) %>% 
      factor(levels = c("Low", "Medium", "High"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Development)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Development))
```

### ii. Distance from Main Stem

Omitting the main stem, let's assess the distribution of distance from main stem values

```{r}
tribs <- dat %>%
  filter(Type != "Main Stem")

tribs
```

```{r}
hist(tribs$Dist_from_EFPC_km, breaks = 386, xaxt = "n")   

axis(
  side = 1,
  at = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = max(dat$Dist_from_EFPC_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    by = 0.25                                           
  )
)
```

Check the quartiles

```{r}
summary(tribs$Dist_from_EFPC_km)
```

Dividing the variable by quartiles (1st and 3rd):

-   \<0.22 km

-   0.22-0.99

-   \>0.99 km

```{r}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Distance_from_EFPC = case_when(
      Type == "Main Stem" ~ "Main stem",
      Dist_from_EFPC_km < 0.22 ~ "<0.22 km",
      Dist_from_EFPC_km >= 0.22 & Dist_from_EFPC_km <= 0.99 ~ "0.22-0.99 km",
      Dist_from_EFPC_km > 0.99 ~ ">0.99 km",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% 
      factor(levels = c("Main stem", "<0.22 km", "0.22-0.99 km", ">0.99 km"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Distance_from_EFPC)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Distance_from_EFPC))
```

### iii. Drainage Area

To classify drainage area (km2) into categories, we'll first inspect its distribution

```{r}
hist(dat$Drainage_area_km2, breaks = 386, xaxt = "n")   # remove default axis

axis(
  side = 1,
  at = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = max(dat$Drainage_area_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    by = 5                                           # tick every 5 km2
  )
)
```

Let's check to quartiles

```{r}
summary(dat$Drainage_area_km2)
```

We'll create categories on whole numbers based on the 1st and 3rd quartiles:

-   \<0.94 km2

-   0.94-11.81 km2

-   \>11.81 km2

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Drainage_area = case_when(
      Drainage_area_km2 < 0.94 ~ "<0.94 km2",
      Drainage_area_km2 >= 0.94 & Drainage_area_km2 <= 11.81 ~ "0.94-11.81 km2",
      Drainage_area_km2 > 11.81 ~ ">11.81 km2",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>%
      factor(levels = c("<0.94 km2", "0.94-11.81 km2", ">11.81 km2"))
  )

# Check
table(dat$Drainage_area)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Drainage_area))
```

### iv. Relative Elevation

To classify relative elevation (m) into categories, we first have to omit 0 values which correspond to the Main Stem

```{r}
tribs <- dat %>%
  filter(Relative_elevation_m != "0")
```

Now we'll first inspect the distribution of relative elevation distribution

```{r}
hist(tribs$Relative_elevation_m, breaks = 386, xaxt = "n")   # remove default axis

axis(
  side = 1,
  at = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = max(tribs$Relative_elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    by = 5                                           # tick every 5 km2
  )
)
```

Check its quartiles

```{r}
summary(tribs$Relative_elevation_m)
```

Breaks at 1st and 3rd quartiles

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Relative_elevation = case_when(
      Relative_elevation_m == 0 ~ "0 m",
      Relative_elevation_m < 2.1 ~ "<2.1 m",
      Relative_elevation_m >= 2.1 & Relative_elevation_m <= 10.5 ~ "2.1-10.5 m",
      Relative_elevation_m > 10.5 ~ ">10.5 m",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ) %>% factor(levels = c("<2.1 m","2.1-10.5 m",">10.5 m", "0 m"))
  )

# Check
summary(dat$Relative_elevation)
```

Check for NAs

```{r}
sum(is.na(dat$Relative_elevation))
```

## V. Save to Excel

Double check before saving

```{r}
View(dat)
```

Bring new variables describing stream inherent characteristics to the front

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat <- dat %>%
  relocate(Type,
           Development,
           Distance_from_EFPC,
           Drainage_area,
           Orientation,
           Relative_elevation,
           .before = pH)

# Check
head(dat)
```

Check the structure one last time before saving

```{r}
str(dat)
```

Save to excel as a clean version of the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet

```{r}
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- "Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean.xlsx"

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create workbook if file does NOT exist
# ---------------------------------------------------------
if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Closed System")
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Closed System", dat)
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)

} else {

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. If the file EXISTS, load it and add/overwrite the sheet
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)

  # Add sheet if missing
  if (!"HA 10% Closed System" %in% names(wb)) {
    addWorksheet(wb, "HA 10% Closed System")
  }

  # Write/overwrite data in that sheet
  writeData(wb, "HA 10% Closed System", dat)

  # Save
  saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}

```

Now repeat this for

-   HA 80% Closed System

-   HA 10% Open System

By replacing the name of the sheet imported and the final excel sheet saved to the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet (first and last code blocks)
